Official Dutch-taught part-time Information Science BSc and programme interests.

curriculum: The 2026–2027 guide confirms the standard Dutch-taught, part-time Information Science BSc and its six learning lines. The 180 EC inventory consists of 55 EC of compulsory foundation courses, 65 EC of later compulsory taught courses (including the 10 EC methods course and 5 EC project preparation), 15 EC restricted choice, 30 EC free electives and a 15 EC final project. The six restricted choices are Python Programming, GIS, Analysing Big Data for Dynamic Systems, Innovation Management, Organizational Consulting and Coaching, and Open Innovation. The guide asks students to choose three across the list. The two groupings are themes rather than formal separate degrees or routes.
progression: Both September and February model rosters place 5 EC of free space among the foundation courses, consistent with the 60 EC foundation threshold for the information science methods course. That threshold includes the academic skills course. The 5 EC foundation elective is within the 30 EC total. Communication Skills requires at least 30 foundation EC, Enterprise Modeling builds on Introduction to Information Science, and Ontology Engineering builds on logic. Software Engineering requires introductory computing, logic, object-oriented analysis and programming, and databases. Graduation Project Preparation follows the rest of the taught program and electives unless the examiner grants permission. It must be completed immediately before the 15 EC independent research project. The standard 10 EC methods course is shown once; the intensive option is an alternative delivery of the same requirement.
components: Choose three courses from the six approved analytics and innovation electives.
Complete 60 EC of foundation study, including the required academic skills course.
Choose eligible courses. The suggested study schedules include 5 EC of electives alongside the compulsory foundation courses.
Complete Graduation Project Preparation immediately before starting the project.
